title: Let your agent revise animations from your team's video notes
summary: Enrico's team has Claude make animations, upload them to the Flask video review tool, read the team's spoken and drawn feedback, and upload revised versions.
agent_role: Claude creates the animation, uploads it with its code, reads timestamped feedback and uploads a new version. Humans give feedback by talking, drawing and sharing screens.
what_they_did: The poster's team uses Claude with custom animation skills and shaders. A connector lets Claude upload each finished animation, with its code and notes, to Flask, a video review tool. Team members leave feedback by talking over the video, drawing on frames and sharing references. Flask passes that feedback back to Claude with exact timestamps.
how_it_went: The source shows Claude applying all feedback points in one pass and uploading a second version. Example points include adding 1.5 seconds, a warmer color grade and moving the key light.
worth_knowing: The poster appears to be from the team behind Flask, so this doubles as a product showcase.
prompt: Create a [length]-second animation of [subject] in the style of [reference]. Save the code and a short change log. Upload the video and its source to [review tool or shared folder]. When I share feedback, read every note with its timestamp. List the changes you plan and wait for my approval. Then apply them and upload it as the next version.

curation.rationale: The post lays out a clear loop: Claude makes an animation, uploads it, takes in recorded team feedback and uploads a new version. It comes from the review tool's own team and reads partly as promotion, with no measured results.
